q.s: A 34-year-old woman with cancer refuses to talk about her prognosis. Instead she lectures the nurses about the molecular pathways of her tumor and the response rates of different drugs. She shows no visible emotion while discussing them.
e: Correct. Using facts and logic to distance herself from distress.
cl: refuses to talk about her prognosis
lectures the nurses about the molecular pathways
q.ch: Serious diagnosis + focus on technical details + no emotion → intellectualization.
q.tr: Isolation of affect separates feelings from events; intellectualization uses facts to do it.
q.q2: Which defense mechanism is she using?

q.s: A 45-year-old man is passed over for a promotion that goes to a younger colleague. He tells his friends that he never wanted the job because the hours would have ruined his golf game. His performance reviews had been poor for 2 years.
e: Correct. A plausible explanation that avoids self-blame.
Wrong. Not attributing his feelings to others.
cl: His performance reviews had been poor
q.ch: Disappointment + acceptable-sounding explanation that hides the true reason → rationalization.
q.tr: "Sour grapes" is the classic example.
q.q2: Which defense mechanism is he using?

q.s: A 6-year-old boy who was toilet trained at 3 begins wetting his pants during the day and asking to drink from a bottle after his parents bring home a new baby. He is otherwise healthy, and urinalysis is normal.
e: Correct. Returning to earlier behaviors under stress.
Wrong. He had progressed beyond this stage.
q.ch: Stressor + return to earlier behavior after mastering it → regression.
q.tr: Fixation means never fully leaving the earlier stage.
q.q2: Which defense mechanism explains his behavior?

q.s: A healthy infant is brought for a well-child visit. She sits without support, transfers a block from one hand to the other and babbles. She cries and clings to her mother when the physician approaches. She cannot yet crawl or wave bye-bye.
e: Correct. Sits, transfers objects, stranger anxiety.
Wrong. Would walk and say words.
cl: transfers a block from one hand to the other
cries and clings to her mother when the physician approaches
q.ch: Sitting + hand-to-hand transfer + stranger anxiety, no crawling → about 6 months.
q.tr: Separation anxiety and object permanence come at about 9 months.
q.q2: What is her most likely age?

q.s: A 9-month-old boy is brought to the emergency department with a swollen right thigh. His father says he fell while walking. X-rays show a spiral femur fracture and healing fractures of several posterior ribs. Retinal exam is normal.
o: Order a vitamin D level only
Report suspected abuse to child protective services
Obtain parental consent to involve social services
Confront the father about the inconsistency
Test for osteogenesis imperfecta before taking any action
cl: healing fractures of several posterior ribs
q.ch: History inconsistent with development + fractures in different stages → suspected physical abuse → mandatory report.
q.tr: Suspicion alone requires a report; confirmation is not needed.
q.q2: What is the most appropriate next step?

q.s: A 9-year-old boy is referred because he cannot finish his schoolwork. His teacher says he blurts out answers, leaves his seat and loses his materials. His parents describe the same behavior at home and at church since age 5. His IQ is normal.
cl: blurts out answers, leaves his seat
q.ch: Hyperactivity + impulsivity + inattention in ≥2 settings before age 12 → ADHD → stimulant.
q.tr: Atomoxetine and α2-agonists are alternatives.
q.q2: Which drug is first-line?

q.s: A 2-year-old boy does not respond to his name and has not started using words. He avoids eye contact and spends hours spinning the wheels of a toy car. He becomes very upset when his daily routine changes. Hearing testing is normal. His head circumference is at the 97th percentile.
o: It is more common in males and associated with increased head size
Intellectual disability is required for diagnosis
It is caused by childhood vaccines
It is more common in females
cl: does not respond to his name
very upset when his daily routine changes
q.ch: Social and communication deficits + repetitive behaviors + restricted interests in early childhood → autism spectrum disorder.
q.tr: Rule out hearing loss first.
q.q2: Which statement about his condition is correct?

q.s: An 11-year-old boy has blinked his eyes forcefully and jerked his shoulders for 2 years. Over the past year he has also started grunting and clearing his throat many times a day. He can suppress the movements briefly but feels an urge to do them. He also washes his hands repeatedly.
e: Correct. Tourette syndrome is associated with ADHD and OCD.
cl: blinked his eyes forcefully and jerked his shoulders
q.ch: Motor + vocal tics >1 year before age 18 → Tourette syndrome → associated OCD and ADHD.
q.tr: For distressing tics: tetrabenazine, antipsychotics or α2-agonists.
q.q2: Which other condition is most commonly associated?

q.s: An 85-year-old man had hip surgery 2 days ago. Tonight he pulled out his IV, is shouting that there are snakes on the floor and does not know where he is. This morning he was calm and oriented. He received diphenhydramine for sleep last night. His temperature is 38.3°C.
o: Search for and treat the underlying cause and stop deliriogenic drugs
cl: there are snakes on the floor
This morning he was calm and oriented
q.ch: Acute fluctuating confusion + visual hallucinations + anticholinergic + fever → delirium → treat cause, remove offending drugs.
q.tr: Delirium is reversible; dementia is chronic with preserved attention early.
q.q2: What is the most appropriate next step?

q.s: A 30-year-old man is found in a bus station 300 km from home. He does not know his name or how he got there. Ten days ago, his wife and son died in a house fire. Neurologic exam, CT and toxicology are normal. He is not seeking any benefit.
cl: He is not seeking any benefit
q.ch: Severe trauma + loss of autobiographical memory + unplanned travel → dissociative amnesia with fugue.
q.tr: Organic causes must be ruled out first.
q.q2: Which diagnosis is most likely?

q.s: A 22-year-old college student has become withdrawn over the past 9 months. He says his roommate is broadcasting his thoughts on the radio and he hears two voices arguing about him. He stopped going to class and rarely showers. His speech is hard to follow. Urine drug screen is negative.
cl: broadcasting his thoughts on the radio
hears two voices arguing about him
q.ch: >6 months of delusions, hallucinations, disorganized speech and negative symptoms → schizophrenia → atypical antipsychotic.
q.tr: Brief psychotic <1 month; schizophreniform 1–6 months.
q.q2: What is the most appropriate first-line treatment?

q.s: A 58-year-old retired teacher has believed for 3 years that her husband is having an affair with their neighbor. There is no evidence. She hires a private investigator and checks his phone daily. She has no hallucinations, keeps her house well, volunteers at church and her speech is organized.
e: Wrong. Functioning preserved, no other symptoms.
cl: believed for 3 years that her husband is having an affair
volunteers at church and her speech is organized
q.ch: Single non-bizarre delusion >1 month + otherwise normal functioning → delusional disorder.
q.tr: Delusional disorder can be shared (folie à deux).
q.q2: Which diagnosis is most likely?
q.fc: Mood chart kept by the patient and her family; dashed line = normal mood (euthymia)

q.s: A 31-year-old woman comes for depression. Her mood chart is shown. During the elevated periods she slept 4 hours a night, felt creative and talked fast for about 5 days, but kept working and was never hospitalized. Her depressed periods lasted about 3 weeks each, with anhedonia, guilt and poor sleep.
cl: kept working and was never hospitalized
q.ch: Hypomanic episodes (≥4 days, no impairment) + major depressive episodes → bipolar II.
q.tr: Antidepressant monotherapy can trigger mania; screen for hypomania before starting.
q.q2: Which diagnosis is most likely?

q.s: A 27-year-old man is brought by police after trying to buy three sports cars with no money. For 10 days he has slept 2 hours a night, talks so fast that he cannot be interrupted and says he has been chosen to end world hunger. He is easily distracted by noises in the hallway.
e: Correct. Mood stabilizer for bipolar I.
cl: trying to buy three sports cars with no money
talks so fast that he cannot be interrupted
q.ch: ≥1 week of elevated mood with DIG FAST features → manic episode → bipolar I → lithium.
q.tr: Atypical antipsychotics, valproate and carbamazepine are also used.
q.q2: Which drug would be most appropriate for long-term relapse prevention?

q.s: A 70-year-old man has lost 9 kg over 3 months, wakes at 3 AM and cannot get back to sleep, and no longer enjoys his garden. He believes his intestines have rotted away and that he is being punished for his sins. He has not eaten or drunk for 2 days and is getting weak.
e: Correct. Psychotic depression with refusal to eat or drink.
cl: has not eaten or drunk for 2 days
q.ch: MDD with mood-congruent psychotic features + refusal of food/fluids → urgent ECT.
q.tr: Otherwise, antidepressant plus atypical antipsychotic.
q.q2: What is the most appropriate treatment?

q.s: Ten days after the delivery of her first baby, a 26-year-old woman tells her husband that the baby is the devil and that God has told her to drown him. She has not slept for 3 days. Her mother has bipolar disorder.
o: Start sertraline and follow up in 2 weeks
Reassure her that this is postpartum blues
Advise her to stop breastfeeding only
Hospitalize her and start an atypical antipsychotic
cl: God has told her to drown him
She has not slept for 3 days
q.ch: Postpartum delusions + thoughts of harming baby + family bipolar history → postpartum psychosis → emergency hospitalization.
q.tr: Postpartum blues: 2–3 days after delivery, resolves within 2 weeks.
q.q2: What is the most appropriate next step?

q.s: A 29-year-old woman has had four episodes over 2 months of sudden pounding heartbeat, sweating, shaking, chest tightness and fear that she is dying. Each episode peaks within 10 minutes. She now avoids driving in case it happens again. ECG, TSH and toxicology are normal.
cl: avoids driving in case it happens again
ECG, TSH and toxicology are normal
q.ch: Recurrent unexpected panic attacks + ≥1 month of worry/behavior change → panic disorder → SSRI + CBT.
q.tr: Benzodiazepines are for short-term acute relief only.
q.q2: What is the best long-term treatment?

q.s: A 24-year-old law student has worried for a year that she will fail, that her parents will get sick and that she cannot pay her loans. She has trouble sleeping, cannot concentrate, feels tense in her shoulders and is irritable with her friends. She has no panic attacks.
e: Correct. SSRI for generalized anxiety disorder.
cl: that she will fail, that her parents will get sick and that she cannot pay her loans
cannot concentrate, feels tense in her shoulders and is irritable
q.ch: Excessive worry about many things ≥6 months + ≥3 CRIMES symptoms → GAD → SSRI/SNRI + CBT.
q.tr: Buspirone, TCAs and benzodiazepines are second-line.
q.q2: What is a first-line medication?

q.s: A 35-year-old man spends 3 hours each morning checking that the doors are locked and the stove is off because he fears his family will die in a fire or robbery. He knows the fears are excessive and wishes he could stop. He is late to work most days.
cl: fears his family will die in a fire or robbery
He knows the fears are excessive and wishes he could stop
q.ch: Intrusive obsessions + compulsions that relieve distress + insight → OCD (egodystonic) → SSRI + CBT.
q.tr: OCPD is egosyntonic: the person sees nothing wrong.
q.q2: Which statement best describes his condition?

q.s: A 32-year-old firefighter pulled a child's body from a burning building 6 weeks ago. Since then he has nightmares, sudden vivid memories of the scene and jumps at small noises. He avoids driving past the street and feels numb with his family. He has started drinking to sleep.
cl: sudden vivid memories of the scene
q.ch: Trauma + re-experiencing + avoidance + hyperarousal + negative mood >1 month → PTSD → SSRI/venlafaxine + CBT; prazosin for nightmares.
q.tr: Symptoms for 3 days to 1 month = acute stress disorder.
q.q2: Which drug specifically helps his nightmares?

q.s: A 26-year-old woman has had a series of intense relationships that end in rage when she feels abandoned. She has cut her wrists several times when upset, spends impulsively and says she feels "empty inside." She tells you that you are the only doctor who understands her and that the previous doctor was evil.
cl: end in rage when she feels abandoned
you are the only doctor who understands her and that the previous doctor was evil
q.ch: Unstable relationships + abandonment fear + self-harm + emptiness + splitting → borderline personality disorder → DBT.
q.tr: Females > males; high suicide risk.
q.q2: Which treatment has the best evidence?

q.s: A 40-year-old man has no close friends and works alone as a night-shift lighthouse keeper. He has never wanted a romantic relationship and seems indifferent when coworkers praise or criticize him. He has no odd beliefs, and his speech is normal.
e: Wrong. Wants relationships but fears rejection.
cl: has never wanted a romantic relationship
indifferent when coworkers praise or criticize him
q.ch: Social withdrawal by choice + emotional indifference without odd thinking → schizoid personality disorder.
q.tr: Avoidant patients want connection but fear rejection.
q.q2: Which personality disorder is most likely?

q.s: A 30-year-old woman wants friends and a partner but turns down every invitation because she is sure people will think she is boring. She switched to a job with no customer contact to avoid criticism. She feels lonely and inadequate.
cl: sure people will think she is boring
q.ch: Desire for relationships + hypersensitivity to rejection + inhibition → avoidant personality disorder.
q.tr: Social anxiety disorder often coexists.
q.q2: Which personality disorder is most likely?
q.fc: Laboratory results during a hypoglycemic episode

q.s: A 32-year-old nurse has had six hospital admissions this year for confusion and sweating from low blood sugar. She does not have diabetes. She asks for more tests and seems eager to have a pancreatic biopsy. She is not seeking time off work or money. Her results are shown.
e: Wrong. Screen negative; C-peptide would be high.
Correct. Secret insulin injection to assume the sick role.
cl: seems eager to have a pancreatic biopsy
She is not seeking time off work or money
q.ch: Hypoglycemia with high insulin + low C-peptide + healthcare worker + no external gain → exogenous insulin → factitious disorder.
q.tr: Symptoms intentional, motivation unconscious (primary gain).
q.q2: Which diagnosis is most likely?

q.s: Three days after watching her father die suddenly of a heart attack, a 19-year-old woman cannot move her right arm. Her reflexes, tone and imaging are normal. When her arm is dropped over her face, it falls to the side and misses. She seems calm and unconcerned about the weakness.
e: Wrong. Not a loss of neurologic function.
cl: falls to the side and misses
q.ch: Acute stressor + neurologic deficit inconsistent with disease + indifference → conversion disorder.
q.tr: Symptoms and motivation are both unconscious.
q.q2: Which diagnosis is most likely?

q.s: A 20-year-old dancer has swollen cheeks below her ears, eroded tooth enamel and small calluses on the backs of her fingers. She admits eating large amounts of food in secret several times a week and then feeling out of control. Her results are shown.
cl: small calluses on the backs of her fingers
eating large amounts of food in secret
q.ch: Binge-purge + normal BMI + parotid swelling + Russell sign + hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis → bulimia nervosa → avoid bupropion.
q.tr: Fluoxetine is the approved drug.
q.q2: Which drug is contraindicated in her treatment?
q.fc: Serum phosphate after admission; dashed line = lower limit of normal (2.5 mg/dL)

q.s: A 17-year-old girl with a BMI of 13.9 kg/m² is admitted with bradycardia and hypotension. She is started on high-calorie feeding. On day 3 she develops muscle weakness, confusion and an irregular heartbeat. Her phosphate levels are shown.
o: Insulin release drives phosphate, potassium and magnesium into cells
cl: muscle weakness, confusion and an irregular heartbeat
q.ch: Severe malnutrition + rapid feeding → ↑ insulin → intracellular shift of PO4, K+, Mg2+ → refeeding syndrome.
q.tr: Start feeding slowly and monitor electrolytes closely.
q.q2: What is the mechanism of her deterioration?

q.s: A 45-year-old man drinks heavily. At a clinic visit he says, "I know drinking is hurting my liver and my marriage, but I'm not sure I can give it up right now. It's how I relax."
o: Tell him he must stop or be discharged
Praise his progress and discuss relapse prevention
Discuss the pros of changing and the cons of continuing to drink
Refer him to inpatient detoxification immediately
Avoid discussing alcohol until he raises it
Set a quit date and prescribe naltrexone today
cl: I know drinking is hurting my liver and my marriage
I'm not sure I can give it up right now
q.ch: Acknowledges problem but ambivalent → contemplation → explore pros and cons.
q.tr: Precontemplation patients deny there is a problem.
q.q2: Which approach best matches his stage of change?

q.s: A 30-year-old woman with depression takes fluoxetine. She is given a drug for a migraine and another for nausea in the emergency department. An hour later she is agitated, sweating and shivering, with diarrhea, a temperature of 39.2°C and rhythmic jerking of her ankles when they are flexed.
cl: a drug for a migraine and another for nausea
agitated, sweating and shivering, with diarrhea
q.ch: SSRI + triptan + ondansetron → serotonin syndrome (3 A's) → benzodiazepines, then cyproheptadine.
q.tr: Clonus and hyperreflexia distinguish it from NMS.
q.q2: Which drug should be given if benzodiazepines and supportive care fail?

head: Finding
Result
Reference
rows: Blood positive, no RBCs on microscopy

q.s: A 24-year-old man with schizophrenia was given several doses of haloperidol over 3 days for agitation. He is now confused and stiff. His findings are shown.
cl: given several doses of haloperidol over 3 days
He is now confused and stiff
q.ch: Antipsychotic + fever + lead-pipe rigidity + autonomic instability + high CK + myoglobinuria → NMS → dantrolene, bromocriptine.
q.tr: "Malignant FEVER": Myoglobinuria, Fever, Encephalopathy, Vitals unstable, Enzymes, Rigidity.
q.q2: Which treatment is most appropriate after stopping haloperidol?
q.fc: Serum lithium levels before and after a new prescription

q.s: A 52-year-old woman with bipolar disorder has been stable on lithium for 6 years. Her primary care physician started a new drug for high blood pressure. Her lithium levels are shown. She now has vomiting, slurred speech, a coarse tremor and an unsteady gait.
cl: new drug for high blood pressure
vomiting, slurred speech, a coarse tremor and an unsteady gait
q.ch: New thiazide → volume contraction → ↑ PCT Na+ and lithium reabsorption → lithium toxicity.
q.tr: ACE inhibitors and NSAIDs also raise lithium levels.
q.q2: Which drug was most likely started?

q.s: A 19-year-old woman is brought in drowsy 2 hours after taking a full bottle of her mother's amitriptyline. Her findings are shown. Shortly after arrival she has a generalized seizure.
e: Wrong. Not standard; may cause arrhythmia.
cl: a full bottle of her mother's amitriptyline
q.ch: TCA overdose + anticholinergic signs + wide QRS + seizure → Na+ channel blockade → sodium bicarbonate.
q.tr: "Tri-C-cyclics": Convulsions, Coma, Cardiotoxicity.
q.q2: What is the most important next treatment?

q.s: A 48-year-old man is admitted for a broken leg. Three days after admission he becomes agitated, sweaty and tremulous. He is picking at the bedsheets, says spiders are crawling on the wall and does not know where he is. His heart rate is 134/min and BP 172/100 mm Hg. His wife says he drinks a bottle of vodka daily.
o: Long-acting benzodiazepine, such as diazepam or chlordiazepoxide
cl: says spiders are crawling on the wall
does not know where he is
drinks a bottle of vodka daily
q.ch: Heavy drinker hospitalized + 2–4 days without alcohol + delirium + autonomic hyperactivity → DTs → long-acting benzodiazepine.
q.tr: Give thiamine before glucose.
q.q2: What is the most appropriate treatment?

q.s: Police bring in a 23-year-old man who was fighting several officers at once. He is extremely agitated and shouting nonsense. His findings are shown. Urine screen is negative for opioids, cocaine and amphetamines.
e: Wrong. LSD; no nystagmus or violence.
cl: negative for opioids, cocaine and amphetamines
q.ch: Violence + nystagmus + hypertension + analgesia → PCP → NMDA antagonist.
q.tr: Vertical nystagmus is a strong clue to PCP.
q.q2: What is the mechanism of the drug he most likely used?

q.s: A 21-year-old woman is brought from a music festival with confusion, clenched jaw and teeth grinding. Her temperature is 40.1°C. She drank many liters of water during the night. Her sodium is 119 mEq/L.
q.ch: Party + bruxism + hyperthermia + hyponatremia (water intake, ADH) → MDMA.
q.tr: MDMA reverses SERT > DAT, NET and can cause serotonin syndrome.
q.q2: Which drug did she most likely take?

q.s: A 38-year-old man with depression has not responded to two SSRIs. He has gained weight on them and is unhappy about their sexual side effects. He also wants to stop smoking a pack a day. He has no history of seizures or eating disorders.
e: Correct. NE/DA reuptake inhibitor; less sexual dysfunction and weight gain, aids smoking cessation.
cl: unhappy about their sexual side effects
stop smoking a pack a day
no history of seizures or eating disorders
q.ch: Depression + SSRI side effects + smoker without seizure risk → bupropion.
q.tr: Bupropion is contraindicated in bulimia and anorexia nervosa.
q.q2: Which antidepressant is most appropriate?

q.s: A 36-year-old woman with treatment-resistant schizophrenia is started on clozapine. Six weeks later she has a sore throat and fever of 39°C.
q.ch: Clozapine + fever and sore throat → check ANC for agranulocytosis.
q.tr: Clozapine also causes seizures, myocarditis and hypersalivation.
q.q2: Which test is the most important to order now?

q.s: A 64-year-old man has taken fluphenazine for schizophrenia for 15 years. His family notices that he constantly smacks his lips, pokes his tongue out and makes chewing movements. The movements worsen when he is anxious.
e: Wrong. Masks temporarily, worsens long term.
Correct. VMAT2 inhibitor for tardive dyskinesia.
cl: taken fluphenazine for schizophrenia for 15 years
smacks his lips, pokes his tongue out
q.ch: Years of D2 blockade + orofacial chorea → tardive dyskinesia → valbenazine or deutetrabenazine.
q.tr: Order of EPS: ADAPT — Acute Dystonia, Akathisia, Parkinsonism, Tardive dyskinesia.
q.q2: Which drug is most appropriate?

q.s: A 41-year-old woman has depression with prominent anxiety and insomnia. She has lost 8 kg because she has no appetite. She wants something to take at night.
o: Bupropion; NE and DA reuptake inhibitor
Mirtazapine; α2 antagonist that increases NE and 5-HT release, with H1 blockade causing sedation and appetite
e: Wrong. Sedating but not used as antidepressant at low dose.
cl: lost 8 kg because she has no appetite
q.ch: Depression + insomnia + weight loss → mirtazapine ("munch more and move less").
q.tr: Mirtazapine's sedation is stronger at low doses.
q.q2: Which drug is most appropriate, and how does it work?

q.s: A 26-year-old man has used heroin daily for 3 years and wants treatment. He last injected 4 hours ago. He is given his first dose of sublingual buprenorphine in the clinic. Within an hour he has yawning, a runny nose, abdominal cramps, diarrhea and goosebumps.
o: He had a delayed heroin overdose
Buprenorphine is a full agonist overdose
Buprenorphine is a high-affinity partial agonist that displaced heroin from μ receptors
The naloxone component was absorbed sublingually
cl: yawning, a runny nose, abdominal cramps, diarrhea and goosebumps
q.ch: Recent full agonist + buprenorphine → displacement at μ receptors → precipitated withdrawal.
q.tr: Wait until mild withdrawal begins before starting buprenorphine.
q.q2: Why did this happen?
